findings.title: #848: the onReactivated re-read is claimed as proven, but the evidence measures the press
findings.evidence: The brief's desired behaviour reads 'asserts the banner converges to the active state AND the detail re-reads (the onReactivated contract)'. The wiring is apps/web/components/work/work-detail.tsx:1307 `onReactivated={onConverge}` and :547 `onConverge={() => state.reload()}`. The walk cell (apps/web/e2e/journal-work-walk.spec.ts:827-857) reads back `state.egressReactivateOpKeys` through the new `egress_reactivate_keys` control op — but that array is pushed inside the `reactivate_client_egress_purpose` handler itself (apps/web/e2e/journal-work-mock.mjs, `state.egressReactivateOpKeys.push(body.p_op_key)`), so it records the PRESS reaching the door, not any subsequent re-read. The spec's own comment at line 849 ('the press told the page to re-read, which reached the runtime proxy exactly once') and the lane report ('(the onReactivated contract) exactly one real, non-empty op key reached the door') both attribute the re-read to that evidence. journal-work-mock.mjs holds no read counter (a grep for a read/poll counter on `state.` returns nothing), so nothing in the suite observes the reload. The cell passes (ok 61 on the reviewer's re-run) — it is simply silent on this half.
findings.required_fix: Either add a read counter to journal-work-mock.mjs symmetric with `egress_reactivate_keys` (count the Work read the detail issues and assert it increments by one across the press), or strike the 'onReactivated contract' claim from journal-work-walk.spec.ts:849 and from the final report and record AC1's re-read half as not covered.

findings.title: #848 AC3: the owner floor is simulated at the wire, so neither branch of the OR is delivered literally
findings.evidence: AC3 reads 'The mock enforces owner-only dispatch, OR the door refusal renders when a lower rank is forced.' What is delivered: the cell arms `state.egressReactivateAnswer = 'denied'` through the control endpoint (apps/web/e2e/journal-work-walk.spec.ts:884) and the mock returns CLR04 on that flag alone, never inspecting the caller (apps/web/e2e/journal-work-mock.mjs). No lower rank is forced. Branch (b) is genuinely unreachable through the browser: the control is owner-gated in the UI (work-detail.tsx:543 `canReactivateEgress={ownerHere}`, :1306 `egressRefused && canReactivateEgress`), so a bookkeeper persona would never see the button. Branch (a) WAS achievable: the harness already derives a lower rank from the sign-in email (apps/web/e2e/serve-built.mjs:598-599 and :611-612 — a `bookkeeper@` prefix gives role_rank 1), so the mock could have read the same persona and answered CLR04 for a non-owner. The lane states the substitution honestly in its report.
findings.required_fix: Either derive the CLR04 answer from the signed-in persona in journal-work-mock.mjs (mirroring serve-built.mjs's own email-prefix rank), or record on #848 that AC3 was met by simulating the wire answer rather than by enforcement, so the criterion is not ticked as written.

findings.title: #863 AC1: the synthetic source is never carried through to a collision, only to verb extraction
findings.evidence: AC1 asks for a cell that feeds the census a synthetic mock source using a non-standard dispatch spelling AND an undeclared shared verb, red before the widening and green after. The four cells delivered (apps/web/e2e/e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts, the 'RPC-opener census · …' group) all assert that `verbsInSource(synthetic)` returns the expected verb list; none reaches `verbCollisions`. That composition was cheap: `verbCollisions(census, declared)` already takes a plain Map, and the same file's existing 'verb-ownership census POSITIVE CONTROL' cell builds one by hand. The substance was verified independently by the reviewer: under the old three-shape opener intake-batch-mock.mjs yields zero verbs, under the new one it yields get_intake_batch, and across all 31 mocks the census grows 136 -> 137 with no owner-set change anywhere. So the blind spot IS closed; only the literal AC-1 cell shape is missing.
findings.required_fix: Add one cell that builds a census from two synthetic sources spelled `rpc === "list_entry_links"` and `path !== "/rest/v1/rpc/list_entry_links"` and asserts verbCollisions flags the undeclared pair, or record the substitution on #863.

findings.title: #862: the body-reader census cannot see this repo's own stream-drain idiom
findings.evidence: PRIVATE_BODY_READER_STREAM only matches `request.on("data"|"end")` — a shape NO lane mock in this repo uses (a reviewer grep over all 31 *-mock.mjs plus mock-dispatch.mjs returns zero hits for `request.on(`). Every real private reader, including all seven this ticket repointed, used `for await (const chunk of request)`, which is caught only incidentally by the function-name half (`function readJson|readBody(`). A new mock writing `async function parseBody(request) { for await (const chunk of request) … }` would pass the census clean. apps/web/e2e/documents-intake-mock.mjs:172-174 already carries an unguarded `for await (const chunk of request) void chunk;` inside `drain()` that the census does not see — deliberate and harmless there, but it is the blind spot standing in the tree. The ticket brief names exactly the two shapes implemented, so this is a literal-AC pass with a known residual hole.
findings.required_fix: Follow-up rather than a blocker: widen the stream pattern to `for await (const chunk of request)` outside mock-dispatch.mjs, with a named exception for documents-intake-mock.mjs's deliberate drain, or file it as an issue against the census.

summary: Six tickets, seven commits, fifteen files, all inside apps/web/e2e plus playwright.config.ts. Five tickets (#862, #863, #865, #902, #853) are DONE against their newest Agent Brief; #848 is PARTIAL. Every claim carrying a ticket was re-run: the census file 33/33, the whole apps/web unit suite 4646 tests / 4644 pass / 0 fail / 2 skip (the lane's counts exactly), typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0, the frozen manifest clean, and the three walks that carry #848, #853 and #902 re-run on the lane's own Playwright triple — 67 passed, 0 failed, with #865's BUILD_ID line printed in that run's own output. Non-vacuity was reproduced independently rather than taken on the report's word, for all four structural tickets: the shipped #862 regexes flag all seven pre-#862 sources; the old three-shape opener finds zero verbs in intake-batch-mock.mjs where the new one finds get_intake_batch, and the widening changes no other owner set (136 -> 137 verbs, no false positives); the pre-#902 handler answers the dedicated client with the empty envelope; the pre-#853 handler returns fourteen rows where the cell demands one. House standards pass: no migration, no frozen-manifest diff, no PRD or ARCHITECTURE edit, no new message key needed (both asserted strings pre-exist in en.json), the manifest already registered, every commit naming its ticket with the required trailer. The one finding that should be settled before #848 is closed is L01-S1: the walk claims the onReactivated re-read, but the op-key read-back it cites records the press rather than the reload, and no read counter exists — either add the counter or drop the claim. L01-S2 (#848's owner floor is simulated at the wire, not enforced, though the UI gate makes the alternative branch unreachable) and L01-S3 (#863's synthetic source is never carried through to a collision) are honest substitutions that should be recorded on their tickets rather than ticked as written.
